# njord

**Design parametric windstorm covers for regions of the UK.**

njord is an R package built entirely on public data: the Copernicus ERA5
windstorm reanalysis, LitPop asset values and a published damage curve. It
turns 86 years of storms (1940-2025) into modelled losses, designs a
parametric cover for a region and measures its *basis risk*: the gap between
what the cover pays and what the layer of losses it stands in for would have
recovered.

![Scotland cover, 1940-2025: payout (on the ramp) and layer recovery by storm against its index. January 2002 (red) has a modelled loss not supported by observed gusts.](man/figures/scotland-cover.png)

## In brief

- **Three ways to set a cover's trigger levels,** each tested out of
  sample: the lowest index among the storms above each loss level
  (`min_index_calibration()`), index levels exceeded as often as those
  losses (`frequency_matching_calibration()`, the recommended rule) and a
  best-fit ramp (`fitted_ramp_calibration()`).
- **Scotland works, in the model's own terms.** In sample, the
  frequency-matched cover pays 18 storms against the 18 that would recover
  (2 false payments, 2 missed), at 1.03 times the layer, with correlation
  0.98. Left out of 17 blocks of five storm seasons in turn, its error is
  0.21 of a flat payout's (90% interval 0.13 to 0.31).
- **England and Wales is harder.** The same rule's out-of-sample error is
  0.78 of a flat payout's (0.55 to 1.11), so the index adds little there.
- **A single UK-wide cover tracks losses poorly:** in-sample correlation
  0.72, against 0.98 for Scotland.

## Status and limits

Work in progress. Basis risk here is measured against a modelled loss built
from the same ERA5 gust field as the index, so the results say how well the
*method* works, not how a cover would pay on real losses. ERA5 gusts differ
from observed station gusts by several m/s for individual storms, and about
a third of the storms the Met Office named in the last ten seasons have no
track in the Hodges product the package uses. The
[vignette](docs/njord-method.md) has the evidence and the planned
refinements.

## Quick start

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("awkward-crow/njord")
```

Run the demos from a clone. They read only the small files in
`inst/extdata/`, so no data download or Copernicus account is needed:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/awkward-crow/njord && cd njord
nix develop --command Rscript inst/demos/calibration_demo.R  # the Scotland cover and plot, seconds
nix develop --command Rscript inst/demos/ciara_demo.R        # Storm Ciara, footprint to loss
```

Without Nix, install R and the packages in `DESCRIPTION` and run the same
scripts with `Rscript`.

## More detail

The [vignette](docs/njord-method.md) covers the data, the damage model, the
trigger and the three rules, all the regions, out-of-sample testing, the
limits above and the planned refinements.

## Use of AI tools

Claude Code (Anthropic) assisted with the code, tests and analysis scripts.
The author specified the method, directed the work and reviewed the
results; the git history carries `Co-Authored-By` trailers.
